_meta.source: Published ENSO teleconnection literature, compiled in docs/research/enso-2026-09/enso_teleconnections.md (2026-09-01). Every row carries its own citation.
_meta.method: NOT fitted here. These are DIRECTIONS AND MAGNITUDES REPORTED IN THE PUBLISHED LITERATURE, transcribed with their citation and the confidence the source itself supports. They are a different KIND of claim from data/enso_model.json, which is this project's own regression on 64 years of FAOSTAT yield. The two are rendered with different encodings on the map and must never be summed, averaged or compared as if commensurate.
_meta.sign_convention: sign = the direction of the EL NINO effect on production in that region. 'dry'/'harm' = negative for output; 'wet'/'benefit' = positive. La Niña is NOT assumed to be the mirror image -- the `la_nina_reverses` field records what each source actually says, and for several regions the answer is 'asymmetric' or 'no'.
_meta.confidence_scale: high | medium | low -- as stated by the cited source, not assigned here. Where a source rates direction and magnitude differently, both are recorded.
_meta.overlap_note: Countries can belong to more than one region (Indonesia: rice and palm; Ethiopia: kiremt and the OND short rains, which have OPPOSITE signs; United States: southern Plains wheat and the Corn Belt; Brazil carries an internal dipole). The map paints a country from its highest-confidence region and the tooltip lists every region it belongs to. A national fill can therefore hide a real sub-national reversal -- this is stated on the page, not hidden here.
_meta.lag_definition: Months from the December ENSO peak to the affected harvest. Negative = the harvest happens BEFORE the peak, i.e. damage occurs during the developing phase.

regions.label: Southern Africa — maize
regions.quantified: Niño3.4 explains 45–53% of seasonal rainfall variance (Funk et al. 2016). r≈−0.53/−0.56 for rainfall. 2015-16: regional maize ~7.2 Mt, 27% below the prior year and 38% below the 5-year average. 2023-24: Zimbabwe maize −72%, Zambia −54%, South Africa yield −17%.
regions.la_nina_reverses: Yes, reliably — the 2020–22 La Niña sequence rebuilt regional stocks.
regions.confidence_note: The strongest and most damaging El Niño signal in the entire literature.

sources.label: Funk et al. 2016 — Assessing the contributions of El Niño and human-induced climate change to the 2015 Ethiopian and Southern African droughts
IFPRI — Southern Africa drought impacts on maize production
WFP — Southern Africa El Niño drought

regions.label: Horn of Africa — OND short rains
regions.quantified: Above-average short rains in only 12 of 20 El Niño events (1901–91). The El Niño signal here is WET — which means flood risk, not simply benefit.
regions.la_nina_reverses: Yes — and the La Niña OND dry signal is the STRONGER of the two.
regions.confidence_note: Sign is opposite to southern Africa, and it flips again by season. A single national colour for the Horn is a simplification.

sources.label: docs/research/enso-2026-09/enso_teleconnections.md — Horn of Africa
ICPAC GHACOF74 — Greater Horn of Africa consensus outlook (OND short rains)
MacLeod et al., Atmos. Sci. Lett. — the OND link is mediated through the IOD, not direct Pacific forcing

regions.scope_note: SOUTHERN Ethiopia only. The OND short rains cover the equatorial south and southeast; the JJAS kiremt highlands, which carry about 85% of Ethiopia's food production, run the OPPOSITE way and are held separately as ethiopia_kiremt. Painting a country one colour cannot show this — the two regions are why Ethiopia's tooltip reports both signs.

regions.label: Ethiopian highlands — JJAS kiremt
regions.damage_season: June–September kiremt (~85% of Ethiopia's food supply)
regions.quantified: 2015: 50–90% local crop loss in worst-hit areas, national cereals −10 to −20%, >75% of the meher crop lost in the worst areas; emergency caseload rose from 4.5 m to 10.2 m in five months.
regions.confidence_note: Directly contradicts the Horn's OND signal in the same country — El Niño wets Ethiopia's Oct–Dec Deyr rains while drying the JJAS kiremt that supplies most of its food.

sources.label: Philip et al. 2018, J. Climate — attribution of the 2015 Ethiopian drought
OCHA — Ethiopia drought response situation report, April 2016

regions.label: Sahel / West Africa — millet
regions.quantified: Millet is affected; maize and sorghum show little or no effect in the same region.
regions.confidence_note: Real but unreliable. Rated low-medium by the source.

sources.label: docs/research/enso-2026-09/enso_teleconnections.md — Sahel

regions.label: Australia — wheat and barley
regions.quantified: −20.8% national yield composite across El Niño years. Individual events: 1994 ~−50%, 2002-03 −58%, 2018-19 crop 23% below the 20-year average, 2023 −36%.
regions.la_nina_reverses: Yes but smaller (+6.5%), and below neutral years.
regions.confidence_note: CRITICAL CAVEAT — direction is high confidence but ENSO ATTRIBUTION IS LOW: residual correlation falls to r = −0.08 once the Indian Ocean Dipole is removed. Much of the apparent Australian El Niño signal is the IOD in disguise. This project's own model assigns Australian wheat NO coefficient for exactly this reason. Australia in 2026 is in fact running wet, against the El Niño script.

sources.label: Impacts of IOD, ENSO and ENSO Modoki on Australian winter wheat yields
The Conversation / ABARES — what El Niño means for wheat

regions.label: India — kharif rice and the summer monsoon
regions.quantified: Monsoon rainfall–Niño3.4 correlation r≈−0.6; drought severity −2.0σ in El Niño years vs −1.3σ otherwise. Base rate of a deficient monsoon in an El Niño year is reported anywhere between 45% and 70% and is genuinely disputed.
regions.confidence_note: Direction is high confidence; magnitude and base rate are low. Transmission to world markets runs through EXPORT POLICY more than through the harvest — India restricted non-basmati rice exports in 2023.

sources.label: IFPRI — India's export restrictions on rice continue to disrupt global markets

regions.label: Indonesia — rice (planting delay)
regions.quantified: A 30-day onset delay produces −11% / −6.5% in the following Jan–Apr harvest; ~1.4 Mt lost per 1 °C of August SST anomaly.
regions.confidence_note: Transmits through AREA PLANTED, not yield per hectare. This project's own yield-based model is blind to it by construction and correctly reports no signal — an absence of measurement, not a finding of no effect.

sources.label: docs/research/enso-2026-09/enso_teleconnections.md — SE Asia rice

regions.label: Philippines — rice
regions.quantified: +1 °C Jul–Sep produces −3.7% irrigated and −13.7% rainfed rice. 2015-16 production −11%.
regions.la_nina_reverses: Not unidirectionally — typhoon behaviour complicates the reverse case.
regions.confidence_note: Strongest for Luzon. Like Indonesia, transmits via area rather than yield.

sources.label: ISEAS Perspective 2023/53 — Rice production and food security in Southeast Asia under threat from El Niño

regions.label: Indonesia & Malaysia — palm oil
regions.quantified: Peak correlation ρ=−0.399. Yield falls 10–14% in year one and a further 3–4% in year two if drought persists. Malaysia 2016: production −13.2% to 17.32 Mt from 19.96 Mt. Indonesia 2016: first annual decline since 1998.
regions.la_nina_reverses: Favourable on balance, but flooding disrupts harvest and haulage.
regions.confidence_note: The longest and best-quantified lag in the ENSO literature — and the strongest, most consistent PRICE channel of any agricultural commodity (Ubilava 2018). The lag is real but probabilistic, not a clock.

sources.label: Impact of El Niño on oil palm yield in Malaysia
MPOB via Malay Mail — El Niño expected to cut palm oil output

regions.label: Central America — Dry Corridor maize and beans
regions.quantified: 2015: national losses −5 to −18%; within the corridor itself 50–100% loss. ~3.5 m people needed humanitarian assistance by June 2016.
regions.confidence_note: Mechanism is high confidence; MAGNITUDE is low — there is no published elasticity for this region.

sources.label: FAO — Dry Corridor situation report

regions.label: Argentina & SE South America — soy and maize
regions.quantified: ENSO explains 72% of Pan-American maize variance. The robust half of this relationship is La Niña HARM, not El Niño benefit: La Niña 2022/23 cut Argentine soy −51%, maize −42%, and 2.2 pp off GDP.
regions.la_nina_reverses: Asymmetric — La Niña harm substantially exceeds El Niño gain.
regions.confidence_note: One of the few regions where El Niño is a measured BENEFIT. This project's own model independently finds Argentine maize +4.5%/ONI.

sources.label: docs/research/enso-2026-09/enso_teleconnections.md — Argentina

regions.label: Brazil — Centre-West, North & Northeast
regions.quantified: 2023/24: Mato Grosso soy yield −16%, national maize −13.8%.
regions.confidence_note: BRAZIL CARRIES AN INTERNAL DIPOLE. In the same 2023/24 season that Mato Grosso fell 16%, Rio Grande do Sul soy rose 68% year-on-year on the wet side of the same event. The national aggregate hides both. Confidence is medium regionally and LOW nationally.

sources.label: docs/research/enso-2026-09/enso_teleconnections.md — Brazil

regions.label: United States — southern Plains winter wheat
regions.quantified: El Niño cuts abandonment by 3 pp; La Niña raises it by 5 pp; an ENSO transition raises it 9 pp in Kansas. The 2023 La Niña-to-El Niño transition produced 32.6% abandonment, the highest since 1917.
regions.confidence_note: The clearest El Niño BENEFIT in the northern hemisphere, and the counterweight to southern Africa. This project's own model independently finds US wheat +4.4%/ONI at q<0.0001 — the single strongest result in the panel.

sources.label: NOAA Climate Program Office — how El Niño flavors affect the region

regions.label: United States — Corn Belt
regions.quantified: Mildly beneficial and WEAK. La Niña raises catastrophic-loss odds in 98%+ of counties; El Niño lowers them in about 72%.
regions.la_nina_reverses: La Niña is the damaging phase here, not El Niño.
regions.confidence_note: Weaker than usually claimed. The damage story for US maize is La Niña, not El Niño.

sources.label: docs/research/enso-2026-09/enso_teleconnections.md — United States

regions.label: Peru & Ecuador — fisheries and coastal flooding
regions.quantified: The strongest and least contested ENSO-economic link anywhere. Anchoveta catch fell from 10.3 Mt (1971) to 4.4 Mt (1972); biomass fell from 5.8 Mt to 1.2 Mt in 1997-98; Peru cancelled the entire first 2023-24 season, with a TAC of 1.09 Mt against a 4.4 Mt/yr non-event average — >$1.4 bn in lost export sales and about 0.5% of Peruvian GDP. Peru's 2023 coastal El Niño cut GDP growth by 1.1 pp.
regions.la_nina_reverses: La Niña is generally favourable for the fishery.
regions.confidence_note: An east-based (coastal) event does its most distinctive damage here, and the 2026 event is currently reading east-based on Niño 1+2.

sources.label: ICES J. Marine Science 2025 — Phenological mismatch contributes to anchoveta landings collapse under El Niño
FAO SOFIA 2024 — impacts on marine fisheries and aquaculture
Banco Central de Reserva del Perú — working papers
